input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariant in haveCommonKSubstring only records non-matching slices str1[x..y] with y <= |str1| - 1, so the last window (x = |str1|-k, y = |str1|) is never covered. Also there is no bound invariant i <= |str1|-k+1. Hence on exit with found == false, the invariant plus !guard cannot establish haveNotCommonKSubstringPred / !haveCommonKSubstringPred (e.g. k = |str1|-1, where the window at i=1 is excluded). Fix: use y <= |str1| and add 0 <= i <= |str1|-k+1."}
EOF
sed -i '100s/.*/\t\tinvariant 0 <= i <= |str1| - k + 1\n\t\tinvariant forall x, y :: 0 <= x < i \&\& found == false \&\& y == x + k \&\& y <= |str1| ==> isNotSubstringPred(str1[x..y], str2)/' program.dfy
sed -n 97,103p program.dfy; dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
program.dfy now verifies: Dafny reports 14 verified, 0 errors.

**What was wrong:** the problem was in a loop invariant, and it showed up as a bridge failure. The loop in `haveCommonKSubstring` checks each length-`k` slice `str1[x..x+k]` to see whether it appears in `str2`. The invariant at line 100 recorded the slices that didn't match, but only those with end index `y <= |str1| - 1`. That left out the last slice, the one ending at `|str1|`. There was also no upper bound on `i`. So when the loop ended with `found == false`, Dafny couldn't conclude that no slice matches, and the postcondition on line 88 failed. The counterexample (`k = 825`, `|str1| = 826`) is a case where the last slice is the one starting at index 1, which was exactly the one left out.

**The fix** (only the loop invariants changed, at lines 100–101):
- I changed the end-index bound from `y <= |str1| - 1` to `y <= |str1|`, so the invariant now covers every slice.
- I added the bound `invariant 0 <= i <= |str1| - k + 1`. Together with the loop exiting, this pins `i` to `|str1| - k + 1`, so every slice has been checked.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before the edit, recording `invariant` / `bridge` with this explanation.
